findings.title: Zero label is positioned at the chart maximum
evidence: All six screenshots place "0 sessions" above the top gridline, opposite "300 sessions at top".
index.html puts both endpoint labels in .scale before .bars; bars grow upward from the bottom baseline.
findings.impact: The scale visually associates zero with the top of a positive-value chart. The baseline explanation and exact table resolve the ambiguity only after reading additional content.
findings.recommendation: Place zero next to the bottom baseline and the maximum next to the top gridline.

findings.title: Weekday abbreviations fragment at enlarged text size
evidence: 375-light-200pct.png and 375-dark-200pct.png split Sat, Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed and Thu across lines.
Independent 375px browser check with root font-size 200% measured .day heights of 107px for those six labels, compared with 61.5px for Fri.
findings.impact: The chart labels become harder to scan even though the page has no horizontal overflow.
findings.recommendation: Keep short weekday labels intact and adapt the chart layout at enlarged text sizes.

verification.runnerChecks: All six reports have no errors, failed requests, overflow, text contrast failures, unlabeled controls or small targets. Runner explicitly excludes charts and interaction semantics from its contrast scan.
independentBrowserChecks: Switched week to month and back; bar counts, heights, ranges, summaries and exact table rows update together.
Week totals independently checked: 1120 selected, 970 previous, +15.5%; peak 8 Oct at 224.
Month totals independently checked: 3794 selected, 3288 previous, +15.4%; peak 2–8 Oct at 1120. All selected buckets exceed corresponding previous buckets.
Opened exact-count disclosure; seven daily rows and four weekly rows match source data and comparison dates.
Explicit Light and Dark selection works. System preference changes work after awaiting the media-query event.
Open exact-count table at 375px and 200% root text size produces no document overflow.
verification.limits: Supplied screenshots show the seven-day view with the exact-count table closed. Month switching and open-table overflow were checked in a browser; no additional screenshots were written.
